purpose: Alternate Radio Station color and material concepts, deliberately distinct from Ceramic Garden. Artistic visualizations, not engine screenshots or exact level geometry.

images.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Standalone landscape 16:9 concept image of RADIO STATION, a playable 3D tank party arena in Godot. One complete image, no collage. Strongly different from a Mediterranean terracotta ceramic garden: NO cream concrete, NO terracotta, NO orange palette, NO beige paving, NO ornamental pottery, NO planters or garden walls, NO coastal Mediterranean architecture. Keep clean friendly stylized low-poly realtime game graphics, chunky bevelled shapes and readable broad combat space. Map topology: two ground-level side courtyards connected by wide end bypasses around a single solid narrow central service terrace 3m high; two broad offset vehicle ramps access terrace from different sides; a conspicuous broadcasting aerial / parabolic antenna on a low compact central base, enough driving clearance beside it. Scattered L-shaped technical barriers, solid radio cabinets and equipment banks break up shots without forming a maze. All main lanes 5-7m wide, ramps at least 6m wide, no mandatory stairs, no narrow catwalks, no roofs over drivable routes. A small cobalt-blue toy scout tank in rear three-quarter foreground, angular enamel hull, separate turret with short cannon, dark rubber tracks, cyan optic, small yellow accents; one or two contrasting red enemy tanks give scale. Tank around2m wide. Actual third-person gameplay camera about9m behind tank, gently looking downward across courtyard, horizon visible. Crisp moderate detail, achievable game geometry, cheerful competitive action, soft shadows, minimal effects. No text, HUD, labels, logo, watermark. Art concept, not actual engine capture. Variant POLAR SIGNAL. Dramatically cool fresh blue and lime visual identity. Deep steel-blue deck, pale icy-blue equipment casings, navy retaining walls, vivid lime-green edge stripes and small equipment doors. Materials are powder-coated METAL panels, segmented aluminium decking and rubber cable troughs, visibly technical rather than masonry. White angular antenna dish on a navy rotating mount with lime joints; compact navy L-shaped hard cover has icy-blue cap panels. Broad floor markings in lime follow ramps and identify elevation. Bright clear mountain daylight with distant pale rock spires and a few small snow patches OUTSIDE the flat non-slippery arena; do not make the arena floor ice. Blue sky, cool balanced sunlight, no warm terracotta tones anywhere. Camera shows central antenna terrace diagonally and both end-route openings.
